topic: MS PowerPoint (Slide Transitions, Animations, and Views)
description: MS PowerPoint is a popular presentation software used to create engaging and structured slide shows. This topic is a highly scoring and crucial section of Computer Knowledge for competitive exams.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of PowerPoint
sections.description: Fundamental terminology and concepts related to creating and designing a presentation.

key_concepts.explanation: A systematic method of presenting ideas, data, and information to an audience using a sequence of electronic pages.
A single electronic page of a presentation that can contain text, images, audio, video, and graphs.
The dotted outline boxes found on a slide layout where text, charts, or graphics are inserted.

sections.title: Different Views in PowerPoint
sections.description: Various modes available for viewing, editing, and organizing slides efficiently.

key_concepts.explanation: The default view in PowerPoint. It is primarily used for creating, designing, and editing individual slides.
Displays all slides in the presentation simultaneously in a miniature (thumbnail) form. It is highly useful for rearranging, deleting, or adding transitions to multiple slides.
Displays the presentation similarly to a Slide Show but within a resizable window with simple control buttons, rather than occupying the full screen.
Presents the slides in a full-screen mode to the audience exactly as they will appear in the final presentation, hiding all editing tools.

sections.title: Transitions and Animations
sections.description: Visual effects applied to slides and individual elements to make the presentation dynamic.

key_concepts.explanation: The specific visual effect that occurs when you move from one slide to the next during a presentation (e.g., Fade, Wipe, Push).
Special movement effects applied to specific individual elements within a single slide, such as text boxes, images, or shapes.
A sidebar tool that allows users to view, reorder, modify, and manage all the animations applied to the current slide.

sections.title: Important Keyboard Shortcuts
sections.description: Crucial keyboard shortcuts frequently asked in exams regarding slide management and viewing.

key_associations.associated_with: Start Slide Show from the beginning
key_associations.extra_info: Plays the presentation starting strictly from the very first slide.

key_associations.associated_with: Start Slide Show from the current slide
key_associations.extra_info: Plays the presentation starting from the active slide you are currently working on.
Stops the running slide show and returns the user to the Normal view.
Adds a new blank slide immediately after the currently selected slide.
Creates an exact identical copy of the currently selected slide.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Direct one-liner facts and technical details regarding MS PowerPoint.

important_facts.fact: When a new blank file is created in MS PowerPoint, the default file name assigned by the system is 'Presentation1'.
The default file extension for PowerPoint 2007 and newer versions is '.pptx', whereas for older versions (up to 2003) it was '.ppt'.
The maximum zoom percentage allowed in MS PowerPoint is 400%, and the minimum zoom percentage is 10%.
During an active Slide Show, pressing the 'B' key instantly turns the screen black, and pressing the 'W' key turns the screen white.
